pron.heading: Pronunciation tip
pron.final: For the end of word or before consonant, final consonant wey be tense or aspirated stop, s, j or ch (k-, t-, p-types and sibilants) dey sound like plain k, t or p, for example {ex}.
pron.liaison: When single or double final consonant follow particle, ending or suffix wey start with vowel (dem write am with silent initial consonant), the final consonant dey sound like the start of the next syllable, for example {ex}.
pron.nasal: Final stop sound (k, t or p type) dey change to nasal sound (ng, n or m) before nasal consonant (n or m), for example {ex}.
pron.lateral: When n sound and l/r sound meet for syllable border, dem dey usually sound like l (small exceptions dey), for example {ex}.
pron.tense: After final stop sound (k, t or p type), the next plain consonant (g, d, b, s or j type) dey sound tense, for example {ex}.
pron.source: Source: Standard Pronunciation Rules of Korean, article {art} (National Institute of Korean Language).
pron.note: This tip dey explain rule. Your device voice na just to play sound; this app no dey judge how you dey pronounce am.
